clue.text: Working left to choice-about time!

indicators.note: about means the phrase for something left to choice goes around the word for time

parts.note: something left to choice is optional
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An exclamation about being given a choice of deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ERA inside OPTIONAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that is working is in service, up and running.

clue.text: In favour of quietly giving support

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Agreeing quietly while lending a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a support or brace.

clue.text: Managed little county farms

parts.note: to run is to manage, so ran is managed
Ches is the short form of Cheshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Someone ran small rural holdings in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranches are large farms raising livestock.

clue.text: Got even-joined up

definitions.meaning: a match that is ... ends level, with equal scores
something knotted or fastened together has been ...

explanation.surface: Settled the score by enlisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Drew level in a contest, and fastened with string or a knot.

clue.text: Like an overcoat that's shabby?

definitions.meaning: an overcoat is worn on the outside of other clothes

explanation.surface: Asking whether an overcoat looks threadbare.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer describes a coat worn outside other clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn on the outside, and worn until threadbare.

clue.text: Yielding to the French quarter. Such a pity!

parts.note: a la is French for to the
S is south, one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Lamenting surrender to France in one district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yielding' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation expressing sorrow or regret.

clue.text: A medical man in the main

definitions.text: A medical man in the main

parts.words: A medical man in the main
parts.note: the main is the sea, so this is a physician aboard a vessel

explanation.surface: A doctor who is mostly a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly', but the main is the high seas.
explanation.definitionFit: A physician serving on a vessel at sea.

clue.text: Plants in pots. A site must be prepared for them

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: potted plants need a spot readied for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be prepared' rearranges the letters of IN POTS and A SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Poinsettia is a Christmas plant with red bracts, here in the plural.

clue.text: Put in place before it's over maybe

definitions.meaning: to place something in position in advance
over is a word such as on, under or with, governing a noun

explanation.surface: Positioning something ahead of time before it finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' looks like 'finished', but it is an example of a part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To place in advance, and a part of speech like over.

clue.text: The alarm at the entrance

parts.note: the entrance is an actor walking on in a theatre, and the alarm is the nerves felt

explanation.surface: A burglar alarm by the front door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a doorway, but it is a performer coming on before an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervousness felt by a performer facing an audience.

clue.text: Resolved never to muse-so bold

indicators.note: resolved read as re-solved means worked out again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone decides never to reflect, being so daring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' rearranges the letters of NEVER TO MUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Daring and willing to take risks.

clue.text: Chance receiving the right instrument

indicators.note: receiving means the word for chance takes in the abbreviation

parts.note: hap is an old word for chance or luck

explanation.surface: An opportunity to get the correct musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' puts R inside HAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed musical instrument plucked by hand.

clue.text: A beastly place, the Orientmake complaint

parts.note: a sty is a pen where pigs, beasts, are kept
E stands for east, the Orient

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a pigsty in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: A complaint is also an ailment; a stye is a small swelling on the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor ailment or disorder of the eyelid.

clue.text: Go off with food or flowers

parts.note: to pop is to go off with a bang
pies are a food

explanation.surface: Choosing between a bang, a meal and a bunch of flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-petalled plants of the genus Papaver, remembrance blooms.

clue.text: Socialist leader invariably cut

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Socialist

parts.note: ever means always, invariably

explanation.surface: A left-wing leader always slashes budgets.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever is to cut through or apart.

clue.text: Man on board having the wind up?

definitions.meaning: a draughtsman is a piece moved on a checkered board in the game of ... (checkers)
a current of cold air blowing through a room is a ...; ... are also drinks downed

explanation.surface: A sailor who gets nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor; it is a counter in draughts, the British name for checkers. 'Having the wind up' suggests fear, but it means a gust of air.
explanation.definitionFit: A game piece in checkers, and a current of air.

clue.text: Unfashionable cleric accepting a note

indicators.note: accepting means the cleric's letters take the others inside

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a cleric
te is a note in sol-fa

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned vicar takes a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts A and TE inside DD.
explanation.definitionFit: Out of date, no longer in style.

clue.text: Fight litter

definitions.meaning: the Battle of ... (1870) was a decisive fight in the Franco-Prussian War
a litter is an enclosed chair carried on poles

explanation.surface: Squabbling over rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous 1870 battle, and a carried chair on poles.

clue.text: A number remains, so hurry!

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Telling someone a figure is left over, so they must be quick.
explanation.definitionFit: To dash is to rush or run quickly.

clue.text: A little iced loaf-a round one-that's way-out

indicators.note: a little of the following words means only some of their letters are used

explanation.surface: Describing a small round iced cake as eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little' indicates a run of letters inside 'loaf-a round'.
explanation.definitionFit: Far away, at a great distance, so a long way off.

clue.text: Were distracted about noon, only to begin again

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the abbreviation
distracted means confused, so the letters of the word are mixed

explanation.surface: People were preoccupied around midday and had to start over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distracted' turns WERE into REEW, and 'about' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to resume or restart something.

clue.text: Rate possibly about the wrong wine being served

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters surround the word for wrong
possibly signals the letters may be arranged differently

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Assessing the poor wine being poured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' turns RATE into RETA, and 'about' puts SIN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Area of Ireland providing Scottish town with base

parts.note: Wick is a town in the far north of Scotland
low means base or mean

explanation.surface: An Irish county gives a Scottish town a foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicklow is a county in eastern Ireland, south of Dublin.

clue.text: A malicious woman being doubly hesitant, he will offer the menu

parts.note: a cat is slang for a spiteful woman

indicators.note: doubly means the hesitation sound appears twice

parts.note: er is the sound made when hesitating

explanation.surface: A spiteful, stammering woman hands out the bill of fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' repeats ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A caterer supplies food for functions, offering dishes to choose from.

clue.text: Diana's the girl to make cashier

parts.note: Di is short for Diana, so Diana's is Di's
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Diana is the young woman to put on the till.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cashier' looks like a bank clerk, but here it is a verb meaning to sack someone, especially from the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To cashier is to discharge or sack someone from service.

clue.text: Music maker finding nothing in order

indicators.note: in means the letter for nothing is placed inside the honour

parts.note: OBE is the Order of the British Empire
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A musician finding everything tidy with nothing to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: OBE is a British honour, Officer of the Order of the British Empire.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument with a double reed.

clue.text: The point is seen in time, as this demonstrates

indicators.note: is seen in signals letters showing within the next words

explanation.surface: A point is visible over time, as this example shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is seen in' signals the letters run across 'time, as this'.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four cardinal compass directions.

clue.text: Shakespearean character taking up arms

indicators.note: taking up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: guns are arms, weapons

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare figure takes up weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: Snug is the joiner in A Midsummer Night's Dream who plays the lion.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug the joiner is a comic figure in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: A man may start to attract attention

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of may

explanation.surface: A man might begin something to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A throat-clearing sound made to catch someone's notice.

clue.text: Grey will have a shot

parts.note: a shy is a throw or attempt, a shot

explanation.surface: An old man will have a try.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash-coloured, pale grey like cinders.

clue.text: Patriot giving people catalogue

parts.note: a nation is a people
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A patriot handing a population an inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: A nationalist is a zealous supporter of their own country.

clue.text: Prison practices outside one's experience?

definitions.meaning: a well-known jail in Manchester, England
unfamiliar habits are odd customs, or unusual methods

explanation.surface: Prison life involves unfamiliar habits.
explanation.walkthrough: The Manchester prison's name read as two words means peculiar customs.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manchester jail, and odd unfamiliar customs.
